title: Power Intent Studio: Open-Source UPF/CPF Authoring from GUI — looking for feedback from ASIC/SoC engineers
author: S
text:
M

MikeSpyke17
New member

Hi everyone,

I recently open-sourced a project called Power Intent Studio, and I’d be very interested in feedback from engineers working with UPF, low-power design, verification, and EDA.

The motivation is fairly simple: power intent becomes difficult to understand and maintain when the RTL hierarchy, power architecture, and UPF are effectively being viewed as separate things.

Power Intent Studio elaborates the actual RTL hierarchy and allows the power architecture to be created or inspected directly on top of it.
Currently it can work with Verilog, SystemVerilog and VHDL designs, as well as Liberty black-box macros. It supports power domains, supply sets, power switches, isolation, retention, level shifters and power states. Existing UPF can also be loaded and mapped back onto the RTL hierarchy, and the resulting power intent can be exported as UPF or CPF.

I open-sourced Power Intent Studio so others can contribute and help extend it. One direction I’d like to explore is power-intent validation, such as detecting missing isolation or invalid domain crossings.

Any technical criticism, suggestions, or real-world use cases would be very welcome.
